name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v6
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
          cache: "pip"
      - name: Build sdist and wheel
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip build
          python -m build --sdist --wheel --outdir dist
          shopt -s nullglob
          wheels=(dist/*-py3-none-any.whl)
          sdists=(dist/*.tar.gz)
          if [[ ${#wheels[@]} -ne 1 || ${#sdists[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
            echo "expected exactly one wheel and one sdist" >&2
            ls -l dist || true
            exit 1
          fi
          python -m venv /tmp/rel
          /tmp/rel/bin/pip install --upgrade pip
          /tmp/rel/bin/pip install "${wheels[0]}"
          /tmp/rel/bin/python -c "import keturah; print('keturah ok')"
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: |
            dist/*.whl
            dist/*.tar.gz
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1

# Changelog

## [Unreleased]

## [0.5.1] — 2026-08-21

### Fixed
- MCP ``server_version`` comes from the installed package, not the literal
  ``0.1.0``. Starting without a family registry prints a stderr banner before
  the demo echo server.

## [0.5.0] — 2026-08-08

Review action for `docs/review-2026-08-08.md` (0.4.0 baseline).

### Fixed
- **H1 / F1**: Stage 0 fields fully enforced — `negotiable` bool, `cost.budget` /
  `cost.budget_class` ∈ `BUDGET_CLASSES`, `evidence.confidence` /
  `evidence.confidence_mode` ∈ `CONFIDENCE_MODES`, `failure_modes` list of
  strings. `capability()` raises `TypeError` on wrong types instead of
  silently coercing (`bool("yes")`, `list("times out")`).
- **H2 / F2**: capability names may not contain `.` (Registry `product.tool`
  separator).
- **M1**: `Registry.to_mcp(namespaced=False)` raises on duplicate tool names.
- **M2**: stdio MCP emits JSON-RPC `-32700` / `-32600` for malformed frames
  instead of silence.
- **M3**: wrong-typed `semantics` / related builder args name the field.
- **M4**: empty product `version` fails `validate_manifest`.
- **L1**: `band_for` maps non-finite values (`nan`, `±inf`) to `unassessed`.

## [0.4.0] — 2026-08-07

### Added
- Stage 0 contract extensions on `Capability` (all optional, additive):
  `negotiable`, `semantics`, `evidence`, `cost`, `failure_modes`
- MCP tools carry these under `_meta.keturah` when present (round-trip safe)
- `BUDGET_CLASSES` / `CONFIDENCE_MODES` vocabularies for validation
- **Layered confidence in `keturah.envelope`**, adopted from `deborah.contracts`
  so the estate has one vocabulary: three dimensions (`evidence`, `inference`,
  `execution`) with ordinal bands (`high`/`medium`/`low`/`unassessed`).
  `SpecialistResult.confidence_bands` carries the decomposition;
  `confidence_layered()` derives it from the legacy scalar when unset. The
  scalar is **never** back-computed from bands — that would manufacture the
  precision the model exists to avoid. `band_for()` matches
  `milcah.deborah.confidence_band` exactly, verified by test.
- **New `keturah.envelope`** — the shared capability-call contract
  (`SpecialistRequest`, `SpecialistResult`, `SPECIALIST_MODES`,
  `TERMINAL_REASONS`, validators). Extracted from two hand-maintained copies
  (`tirzah.coherence`, `milcah.contract`) that had already drifted: only the
  consumer carried `error`/`error_type`, so a provider could not represent its
  own failure. Both now import one definition.
- **New `Evidence` type** (`kind`/`ref`/`note`) plus `normalise_evidence()`.
  Evidence was `list[str]`, so "evidence-backed" could be asserted but never
  checked. `SpecialistResult.is_anchored` distinguishes evidence that points at
  something from prose. Bare strings still work — they upgrade to `kind="note"`,
  so no producer has to change first.
- `Registry.find_all()` now parses namespaced `product.tool` names the same way
  `find()` does — `find_all("milcah.coherence_check")` returned `[]` before (#10).
  It also takes the `product=` keyword for symmetry with `find()`.
- New federated `Registry.resources()` and `Registry.prompts()`, mirroring the
  per-manifest accessors across every product (#13).

## [0.3.0] - 2026-07-10
- Hanani handlers wired into the MCP server.
- `list only executable tools` — non-tool capabilities no longer surface as
  callable MCP tools.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-07-06
- Minimal stdio MCP server for family tools (Codex / Claude Code), with the

- `outputSchema` in the MCP projection, `schema_version` + stricter validation,

# Keturah

**Keturah describes what an LLM can call in your product, once, in a form
that is also MCP.** Each interface is a `Capability` (name, description,
JSON-Schema input and output); a `Manifest` bundles a product's capabilities
with its name and version; a `Registry` lets agents discover capabilities
across many products. `to_mcp()` turns any of them into the Model Context
Protocol `tools/list` shape, so an MCP server becomes a thin adapter over the
manifest rather than a second definition that can drift.

It is pure stdlib with no dependencies. The name means "incense, that which is
offered up": the catalogue of what each product **offers**.

## Is it for you?

**Good fit:** you have several libraries or services, not just MCP servers,
and want one description of their LLM-callable interfaces that drives
discovery, validation and MCP from the same source. In this family the
manifests are built from contracts each product already enforces (Deborah's
plan schema, Milcah's specialist request and result, Galeed's events).

**Not a fit:** you only need a single MCP server. Use an MCP SDK directly.
Keturah's own server is minimal and implements tools only (see below).

## Try it

```bash
pip install keturah
keturah-mcp --demo        # a stdio MCP server with two demo tools
```

Register it with an MCP client, for example
`claude mcp add keturah -- keturah-mcp --demo`, and the client can list and
call `demo.echo`.

Describe your own product:

```python
from keturah import manifest, capability, Registry

m = manifest(
    "tirzah",
    version="1.3.0",
    capabilities=[
        capability(
            "ask",
            "Answer a question over Tirzah's memory.",
            input_schema={"type": "object",
                          "properties": {"query": {"type": "string"}},
                          "required": ["query"]},
            output_schema={"type": "object",
                           "properties": {"answer": {"type": "string"}}},
            tags=["qa", "memory"],
        ),
        capability("system_prompt", "Default system prompt for agents.", kind="prompt"),
    ],
)

m.to_dict()        # the full manifest, with descriptions and schemas
m.to_mcp()         # MCP tools/list: tools only, including outputSchema
m.prompts()        # kind="prompt" capabilities (also: m.resources())
```

A product usually exposes this as `capabilities()` and, if it is a service, as
`GET /api/capabilities` (`?format=mcp` for the MCP view).

## Discovery across products

```python
reg = Registry([m, other_manifest])

reg.find("tirzah.ask")             # namespaced, the form to_mcp() emits
reg.find("ask", product="tirzah")  # or by explicit product
reg.find_all("ask")                # every product exposing that name
reg.with_tag("planner")            # also: tools(), resources(), prompts()
reg.to_mcp()                       # union tools/list, named product.tool
```

## Mapping to MCP

| Keturah | MCP `tools/list` |
|---|---|
| `name` | `name` (a Registry emits `product.tool`) |
| `description` | `description` |
| `input_schema` | `inputSchema` |
| `output_schema` | `outputSchema` (omitted when unset) |

Only `kind="tool"` capabilities are projected. Resources and prompts stay on
the Keturah surface (`resources()` / `prompts()`).

## Serving over MCP

`keturah.mcp.run_stdio_server(registry, handlers={...})` runs a minimal,
synchronous stdio MCP server. It implements `initialize`, `tools/list` and
`tools/call`. It lists only tools that have a handler, and does not serve MCP
resources or prompts.

`keturah-mcp` with no flags serves the family registry from an installed
Tirzah, with whichever handlers Tirzah and Hanani provide; `--demo` needs
nothing installed.

## Calling a capability: the envelope

`keturah.envelope` defines the shape of one call and its result:
`SpecialistRequest`, `SpecialistResult`, `Confidence` and `Evidence`, with
`validate_request` / `validate_result`. Evidence has a `kind` and a `ref`, so a
validator can check that it points at something. `normalise_evidence` upgrades
older free-text evidence lists, so existing producers keep working.

## Versioning

Manifests carry `schema_version`, and validation requires it to equal
`MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` (currently `"1.0"`), so consumers can version-gate.

## Develop

Stdlib-only, so it behaves the same on Linux and WSL.

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest
```

# Keturah — functional and code review

**Date:** 2026-08-08 · **Reviewed:** `master` @ `b3ec8a7`, version **0.4.0**
(clean working tree)
**Method:** the public API was exercised directly (manifest → MCP projection →
registry federation), the envelope invariants were probed adversarially, and the
stdio MCP server was driven with well-formed and malformed JSON-RPC. Then the
source was read. Every claim below is backed by a run or a probe, reproduced
inline.

> **Disclosure.** `src/keturah/envelope.py` and `tests/test_envelope.py` were
> written by this reviewer in an earlier session. They are reviewed here on the
> same terms as everything else, and one finding (L1) is against that code.

---

## Part 1 — Functional review

**Baseline:** `39 passed` in 0.04 s. `ruff check src tests` clean, rule set
pinned (`select = ["E4","E7","E9","F"]`) with the explanatory comment, CI gates
both. 1,620 lines total — by far the smallest repo in the estate, and it shows in
the best way.

### What works

The README's examples were run verbatim and all behaved as documented:

```
schema_version: 1.0
to_mcp tools: ['ask']            outputSchema present: True
resources: ['capabilities']      prompts: ['system_prompt']

find('ask')         -> ('tirzah', <Capability ask>)
find('tirzah.ask')  -> ('tirzah', 'ask')
find_all('ask')     -> [('tirzah','ask'), ('milcah','ask')]
reg.to_mcp names    -> ['tirzah.ask', 'milcah.ask', 'milcah.critique']
```

Resources and prompts correctly stay off `to_mcp()`; `outputSchema` is emitted
when set and omitted when not; the Registry namespaces as `product.tool` exactly
as the table promises.

**`validate_manifest` is the most thorough validator in the estate.** Every
adversarial case on the original fields was caught:

```
flagged  duplicate capability names   ['duplicate capability name: ask']
flagged  unknown kind                 ["capability[0] invalid kind: 'wizard' …"]
flagged  empty capability name        ['capability[0] missing name']
flagged  empty product                ['manifest missing product']
flagged  input_schema is a string     ['capability[0] input_schema must be a JSON-Schema object']
flagged  empty description            ['capability[0] (x) missing description']
```

Compare Deborah's `validate_plan`, which accepted duplicate step ids, dangling
dependencies, self-dependency and cycles.

**The shared envelope's documented invariants hold under pressure.** Each was
probed rather than assumed:

```
scalar never back-computed from bands : True
unassessed distinct from low          : True
band thresholds 0.7 / 0.4             : True
band_for(0.0) and band_for(None)      : unassessed

flagged  confidence = 1.4        flagged  confidence = nan
flagged  confidence = -1         flagged  confidence = inf
flagged  terminal_reason bogus   flagged  band bogus
flagged  unknown dimension
```

**The stdio MCP server answers correctly and flushes.** Driven with six frames,
all four valid requests were answered, `tools/call` dispatched to the handler,
and unknown methods returned `-32601`. `_write_json` calls `sys.stdout.flush()` —
the classic stdio-server hang is avoided.

Notably absent: this is the only repo in the estate with **no unanchored
substring matching and no degenerate constant metric**, the two families that
appeared in every other review.

### Functional defects

#### F1. The Stage 0 contract fields are exported as vocabularies and enforced as nothing

`BUDGET_CLASSES` and `CONFIDENCE_MODES` are in the public API:

```python
BUDGET_CLASSES   = frozenset({'free','low','medium','high','unbounded'})
CONFIDENCE_MODES = frozenset({'none','heuristic','calibrated'})
```

None of the fields they govern is validated:

```
ACCEPTED  negotiable = 'yes' (string, not bool)
ACCEPTED  cost budget = 'infinite'          (not in BUDGET_CLASSES)
ACCEPTED  evidence mode = 'vibes'           (not in CONFIDENCE_MODES)
ACCEPTED  failure_modes = 'times out'       (a string, not a list)
```

`validate_capability` returns `[]` for all four. A consumer reading the public
constants will reasonably assume they are enforced, and `failure_modes` as a
string will iterate character-by-character in any consumer that loops over it.

This is the newest release's additions (`b3ec8a7 — Stage 0 contract fields`)
shipping ahead of their validation, in a package whose entire job is being the
place contracts are checked.

#### F2. Capability names may contain the namespace separator

`validate_manifest` accepts a capability literally named `a.b`, and `.` is what
`Registry` uses to separate product from tool. The namespace is therefore not
injective:

```
two manifests: product 'a' with tool 'b', and product 'x' with tool 'a.b'

to_mcp names      : ['a.b', 'x.a.b']
find('a.b')       -> ('a', 'product a, tool b')          ← product x's tool is shadowed
find_all('a.b')   -> [('a','b')]                          ← the other match is OMITTED
find('x.a.b')     -> ('x', "product x / tool 'a.b'")      ← recoverable if you know the product
```

`find_all` is documented as *"every product exposing that tool name"* and here
returns one of two. Nothing warns.

**Exposure is latent, not live** — every family manifest was checked and none
uses a dotted capability name:

```
Tirzah: 6 caps, dotted=none    Hoglah:   2 caps, dotted=none
Milcah: 4 caps, dotted=none    Deborah:  6 caps, dotted=none
Mahalath: 2 caps, dotted=none  Hanani:   6 caps, dotted=none
```

So this is a validation gap to close before it bites, not a live bug.

---

## Part 2 — Code review

### High

#### H1 · `manifest.py` — `validate_capability` does not check the Stage 0 fields

Code side of F1. The function validates `name`, `description`, `kind`,
`input_schema` and `output_schema` thoroughly, then stops. `negotiable`,
`semantics`, `evidence`, `cost` and `failure_modes` — added in 0.4.0 — pass
unchecked.

**Fix:** four checks, all mechanical.

```python
if not isinstance(cap.negotiable, bool): …
budget = (cap.cost or {}).get("budget")
if budget is not None and budget not in BUDGET_CLASSES: …
mode = (cap.evidence or {}).get("confidence_mode")
if mode is not None and mode not in CONFIDENCE_MODES: …
if not isinstance(cap.failure_modes, list): …
```

The envelope already does exactly this for `TERMINAL_REASONS`,
`CONFIDENCE_BANDS` and `CONFIDENCE_DIMENSIONS`, so the pattern to copy is in the
same package.

#### H2 · `manifest.py` / `registry.py` — `.` is a separator and also a legal name character

Code side of F2. `Registry` splits on `.` to resolve `product.tool`, and
`validate_manifest` permits `.` inside a capability name, so a single string can
denote two different (product, capability) pairs. `find_all`'s omission is the
worst consequence because its whole purpose is exhaustiveness.

**Fix:** reject `.` in `Capability.name` in `validate_capability`. That is
strictly safer than making the resolver smarter, and costs nothing today since no
product uses it.

### Medium

#### M1 · `registry.py` — `to_mcp(namespaced=False)` can emit an invalid `tools/list`

```
to_mcp(namespaced=False) names: ['ask', 'ask']
duplicate MCP tool names emitted: True
```

MCP requires unique tool names in `tools/list`; a client will either reject the
response or silently keep one. The default is `namespaced=True` and is correct,
so this only bites the explicit opt-out — but an API that can produce a
protocol-invalid response should say so rather than emit it.

**Fix:** raise (or warn and namespace anyway) when non-namespaced emission would
collide.

#### M2 · `mcp.py:88-94` — malformed frames produce silence, not a JSON-RPC error

```python
try:
    req = json.loads(line)
except json.JSONDecodeError:
    continue                       # ← no response at all

if not isinstance(req, dict):
    continue                       # ← no response at all
```

JSON-RPC 2.0 §4.2 requires `-32700 Parse error` with `"id": null` for the first
and `-32600 Invalid Request` for the second. Verified: six frames in, four
responses out, and the two malformed ones produced nothing. A strict client
waiting on a response to a corrupted frame will block.

`_error_response` is defined at line 42 and used correctly on every other error
path — this is two `continue`s that should be writes.

#### M3 · `manifest.py:156` — a wrong type on `semantics` raises a raw `dict()` error

```
>>> capability("x", "d", semantics="freeform")
ValueError: dictionary update sequence element #0 has length 1; 2 is required
```

`dict(semantics or {})` leaks its internals. Every other bad type is either
accepted (H1) or reported cleanly by `validate_capability`; this one fails at
construction with a message that does not name the field.

#### M4 · `manifest.py` — an empty `version` validates clean

```
ACCEPTED  no version   (manifest("p", version="", …))
```

The README's premise is that *"Manifest validation requires `schema_version`
equal to `MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION` so consumers can version-gate"*, and the
product `version` is part of what a consumer gates on. `schema_version` is
checked; the product version is not.

### Low

#### L1 · `envelope.py` — `band_for` does not range-check

```
band_for(float('inf'))  -> 'high'
band_for(float('nan'))  -> 'unassessed'
```

`validate_result` correctly rejects `confidence=inf` on a `SpecialistResult`, so
the envelope as a whole is sound — but `band_for` is exported publicly and a
producer calling it directly on an unvalidated number gets `high` for infinity.
The `nan` case is right by accident (comparisons with `nan` are all False, so it
falls through to `unassessed`) rather than by design.

**Fix:** return `unassessed` for any non-finite value, explicitly. *(This is the
reviewer's own code.)*

---

## Comparison with the Hoglah, Deborah, Tirzah, Milcah, Mahalath and Hanani reviews

Keturah is the cleanest of the seven, and the only one where neither recurring
family appears:

- **No unanchored substring matching.** Hoglah matched on error text, Deborah on
  construct keywords with `re.I`, Milcah on prose markers. Keturah's only
  string-identity operation is the `.` split, and its failure mode (F2/H2) is
  ambiguity in a namespace, not a wrong match.
- **No degenerate constant.** Hoglah's counters, Milcah's `global_coherence`,
  Hanani's all-`True` audit scores. Keturah has no computed metric to get wrong.

Its own finding is a third thing, and a common one in small well-run packages:
**the newest fields shipped ahead of their validation.** The same file that
validates `TERMINAL_REASONS`, `CONFIDENCE_BANDS` and `CONFIDENCE_DIMENSIONS`
rigorously exports `BUDGET_CLASSES` and `CONFIDENCE_MODES` and checks neither.
So this is not a team that doesn't validate — it is one release of new fields
that outran the validator.

That matters more here than it would elsewhere. Keturah is the package the other
six trust to tell them what a contract is; a vocabulary it exports but does not
enforce is a promise the rest of the estate will build on.

The estate-wide property still holds, in its mildest form: **silence**. An
invalid budget class, a shadowed `find_all` match, a duplicate MCP tool name, a
dropped JSON-RPC frame — none logs or raises.

---

## Suggested order

1. **H1** — four type/vocabulary checks in `validate_capability`. Highest value
   in the estate per line changed, because six products consume these fields.
2. **H2** — reject `.` in capability names. One line, no migration cost (verified
   against all six family manifests).
3. **M2** — replace two `continue`s with `_error_response` writes. The helper
   already exists.
4. **M1, M4, M3** — collision guard, version check, and a clear type error.
5. **L1** — explicit non-finite handling in `band_for`.

Nothing here is architectural. The MCP-projection design is right, the
manifest-from-seam-contracts principle is right, the Registry semantics are
right, and the envelope holds up under adversarial probing. Every finding is a
missing check in a validator that already exists and already does the same job
correctly for its older fields.

# Capability manifests

A `Capability` describes one LLM-callable interface: name, human description,
input/output schema. A `Manifest` collects a product's capabilities and
answers in two dialects: the family's own (`to_dict()`) and MCP
(`to_mcp()` → `tools/list`, names namespaced `product.tool` when federated).

The discipline: manifests are **built from the executable seam contracts**
(each sibling's `<pkg>.manifest.build_manifest()`), not hand-maintained — so
what a manifest advertises is what the tests enforce. Tirzah serves its own at
`/api/capabilities` and the federated family registry at `/api/registry`
(every importable sibling's manifest, lazily and fail-soft); its planner
advertises specialist tools FROM the manifest rather than from prose.

# Keturah

Keturah lets any family product — library *or* service — answer one question:
*what can an LLM call here, and how?* Each interface is a `Capability` (name,
description, input/output schema); a `Manifest` collects them and bridges to MCP
(`to_mcp()` → `tools/list`). Built FROM the executable seam contracts so the
manifest cannot drift from the code.

## Map

- **[Concepts](concepts/index.md)** — the capability-manifest model.

- **manifest** — `Capability`, `Manifest`, `build_manifest()` conventions.
- Family adoption: every sibling exposes `<pkg>.manifest.build_manifest()`;
  Tirzah serves the federated registry at `/api/registry` and its own at
  `/api/capabilities` (`?format=mcp`).

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "keturah"
version = "0.5.1"
description = "Keturah — a uniform, MCP-bridgeable manifest of a product's LLM-consumable interfaces."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = {file = "LICENSE"}
authors = [{name = "gellsmore-svg"}]
keywords = ["llm", "mcp", "tools", "interface", "manifest", "capabilities", "local-first"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Topic :: Software Development :: Libraries :: Application Frameworks",
    "Typing :: Typed",
]
# Dependency-free: the manifest shape is pure stdlib so any product can adopt it.
dependencies = []

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/keturah"
Repository = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/keturah"
Issues = "https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/keturah/issues"

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest>=8"]

[project.scripts]
keturah-mcp = "keturah.mcp:main"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.setuptools.package-data]
keturah = ["py.typed"]

[tool.ruff]
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]

# widened those defaults, which silently turns a green gate red on a tool
# upgrade. This is the historical default set (pyflakes + the pycodestyle
# errors worth gating), so the gate means the same thing on every ruff version.
select = ["E4", "E7", "E9", "F"]
